questions.question: What is the main benefit of placing pasted material inside `<document>` tags and instructions inside `<instructions>` tags?
options: The model processes tagged text faster
It makes clear which text is material to work on and which is the task
Only specific tag names are recognised by the model
Tags reduce the cost per token
questions.explanation: Delimiting separates instructions from data, reducing confusion and making embedded text harder to mistake for instructions.

questions.question: You tagged a contract as `<contract>`. What is the best way to refer to it in your instructions?
questions.explanation: Referring to tags by their exact name removes ambiguity; switch names and the model has to guess.

questions.question: Why ask the model to put its final recommendation in `<decision>` tags?
options: So code can reliably extract the decision from the response
Because the model cannot make decisions otherwise
To hide the decision from the user
To make the model think harder
questions.explanation: Tagged output is easy to read and easy to parse, for example with a simple regular expression.

questions.question: Which statement about "prefilling" the start of Claude's reply is accurate for current models?
options: It is the recommended way to force JSON output
It is required whenever you use XML tags
It is a legacy trick not supported on current Claude models; use format instructions and structured outputs instead
It only works with documents placed at the end of the prompt
questions.explanation: Prefill is not supported on current Claude models; clear format instructions and the provider's structured output feature replace it.
